## Overview

Document how asymmetric connector configurations can cause an effective HMA-state mismatch during the NIXL handshake. Addresses the documentation request in #60124; does not add field-level mismatch diagnostics.

## Claims

- Explain why omitting the HMA flag on both instances need not produce matching effective settings.
- Document supported remedies, HMA-required configurations, and the need to compare other compatibility fields.

## Validation

- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pre-commit run --files docs/features/disagg_prefill.md docs/features/nixl_connector_compatibility.md` — passed.
- `API_AUTONAV_EXCLUDE='re:.*' VLLM_DOCS_BUILD=1 mkdocs build --site-dir <output>` — passed with existing API cross-reference warnings because API generation was excluded.
- Inspected generated HTML: both new anchor links resolve; the HMA note is inside the MultiConnector list item.
- Cross-checked the explanation against connector HMA support detection, config auto-disable behavior, the compatibility hash, and NIXL/HiSparse guards. Documentation-only: no model or GPU evaluation performed, and no end-to-end serving fix claimed.

## Details

MultiConnector requires every child to support HMA. Automatic configuration can therefore disable HMA only on one peer, while the other keeps it enabled. The handshake compares the effective state, not merely whether users supplied the same flags.

The workaround is intentionally conditional: HMA cannot be disabled for the documented SSM/Mamba or HiSparse configurations, and matching HMA alone does not guarantee compatibility. The transfer safety check remains unchanged.

Duplicate checks found no open PR for `60124 in:body` or the same HMA troubleshooting text. #59584 covers authentication/side-channel troubleshooting; #60113 changes heterogeneous KV-group transfer; #48882 changes subclass validation; #42620 implements LMCache HMA support. None supplies this explanation.

AI assistance was used for investigation, drafting, implementation, and automated review/validation. The human submitter reviewed the changes and authorized submission. The validation results above were obtained with AI assistance.

files.patch:
@@ -31,9 +31,13 @@ Now supports 9 types of connectors:
 - **MoRIIOConnector** (ROCm only): see [MoRI-IO Usage Guide](moriio_connector_usage.md) for example usage and detailed documentation.
 - **MultiConnector**: take advantage of the kv_connector_extra_config: dict[str, Any] already present in KVTransferConfig to stash all the connectors we want in an ordered list of kwargs.such as:
 
-  ```bash
-  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"},{"kv_connector":"ExampleConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"shared_storage_path":"local_storage"}}]}}'
-  ```
+    ```bash
+    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"},{"kv_connector":"ExampleConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"shared_storage_path":"local_storage"}}]}}'
+    ```
+
+    HMA support depends on **all** configured children. When combining NIXL with
+    another connector, check that prefill and decode use the same effective HMA
+    state; see [Troubleshooting an HMA compatibility mismatch](nixl_connector_compatibility.md#troubleshooting-an-hma-compatibility-mismatch).
 
 - **OffloadingConnector**: enable offloading of KV data to CPU memory, customizing the CPU block size (in tokens) and total CPU memory bytes to allocate:

@@ -81,6 +81,7 @@ By default, a **compatibility hash** is checked during handshake. P and D instan
 - Model (architecture, dtype, number of KV heads, head size, number of hidden layers)
 - Attention backend
 - KV cache dtype (`cache_dtype`)
+- Effective hybrid KV cache manager (HMA) enabled/disabled state
 - EAGLE/MTP-style speculative method and draft-model configuration
 - NIXL transfer mode (push vs pull) — a push (WRITE) connector and a pull (READ)
   connector use incompatible transfer protocols and must never be paired
@@ -98,6 +99,37 @@ By default, a **compatibility hash** is checked during handshake. P and D instan
   resulting KV block layout is validated at handshake time rather than via the
   compatibility hash)
 
+### Troubleshooting an HMA compatibility mismatch
+
+`NIXL compatibility hash mismatch` means that at least one of the
+[required settings](#what-must-match-between-p-and-d) differs. One possible
+cause is a different effective HMA state, even when both instances omit
+`--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager`.
+
+`MultiConnector` supports HMA only when **every configured child connector**
+supports it. With automatic HMA selection, adding a child without HMA support
+disables the hybrid KV cache manager on that instance and logs
+`Turning off hybrid kv cache manager`. A peer using `NixlConnector` alone may
+keep HMA enabled, causing the handshake to reject the transfer.
+
+To resolve this case:
+
+1. Check the connector configurations and startup warnings on **both** prefill
+   and decode instances, including all `MultiConnector` children.
+2. If the model and enabled features support running without HMA, pass
+   `--disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` to **both** instances and restart them.
+   Otherwise, use HMA-capable connectors on both sides, including every child
+   of a `MultiConnector`.
+3. If the handshake still fails, compare the other required settings above.
+   Matching the HMA state alone does not establish compatibility.
+
+!!! warning
+    Hybrid SSM/Mamba models and HiSparse require HMA; disabling it is not a
+    workaround for those configurations. Disabling HMA can also reduce
+    sliding-window attention efficiency. Do not bypass the compatibility hash
+    check to work around mismatched configurations: it protects against
+    incompatible KV cache transfers.
+
 ### KV cache layout
 
 - NixlConnector defaults to **`LBHNC`** (head-major, formerly `HND`) layout for optimal transfer performance (non-MLA models).
